title: Keyword-sensitivity test of the specificity ratio
question: Is the wisdom/control rate ratio an artifact of which keywords were chosen?
method: 1000 random ontologies sampled from the corpus vocabulary (freq >= 100), each keyword frequency-matched to a real keyword within +-50 frequency ranks; identical 10,000-word chunking as statistical_validation.py
parity_note: Single-word counting uses exact token equality; the regex detector (statistical_validation.py) additionally matches tokens with edge apostrophes (e.g. 'said), giving 1.753x vs 1.707x here. The sensitivity comparison is internally consistent: real and null ontologies use identical counting.
conclusion: Real single-word ontology ratio 1.71x vs frequency-matched null mean 1.07x (95% of nulls below 1.44x); z = 3.4, percentile 99.7, empirical p = 0.0040. The specificity effect is NOT explained by keyword choice or word frequency.
